subject: POC: Prompt set & eval dataset for Redwood trial
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>

Subject: POC: Prompt set & eval dataset for Redwood trial

Hi Alice / Sam —

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation and strong alignment on a focused POC to validate latency, safety, and cost tradeoffs for your triage assistant use case. Recap + ask below so we can lock timelines: 

POC goal (success criteria):
- 90th percentile latency < 600ms for 1- to 3-turn prompts at 1 RPS (your target)
- Safety: false-positive rate on red-flag classifier < 5% on sampled prompts
- Quality: > 85% accept rate on our annotator eval (we'll provide rubric)
- Cost target: <= $X per 1k tokens (we'll model based on your sample prompts)

What we need from you to start:
1) Prompt set: representative prompts (CSV or XLSX) with columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, intent_tag (if available) — attach whatever you have.
2) Chat logs (optional but ideal): 2-3k anonymized conversations or recent query logs (we can accept sanitized JSON). If logs contain PHI, please redact or flag as sensitive and we will handle per our Data Handling Addendum.
3) Owner / point of contact on your side for technical onboarding and procurement contact for contracts.

Proposed timeline:
- Feb 9: kickoff workshop (30-45 min) + confirm ownership and success criteria
- Feb 9–13: ingestion & baseline runs on your prompts
- Feb 16: results review + model/config recommendations

Notes on data handling: We'll only use the dataset for this POC and will delete after 90 days unless you request extended retention. We can sign any necessary DPA/NDA — please share procurement contact if needed.

I've attached a short POC Eval Plan (redwood_poc_eval_plan.pdf) that outlines the evaluation rubrics and the two model configs we typically run for triage workloads.

Next steps: Please send the prompt file and/or logs, confirm the internal POC owner at Acme Health, and let me know availability for a Feb 9 kickoff (AM or PM PST).

Thanks — looking forward to getting this going.

—
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Thanks Alice — this is perfect and exactly what we need to start. Answers to your questions and a slight update to the plan below.

Quality rubric / annotations: we'll provide a shared Google Sheet with the annotation template, but briefly we'll ask annotators to label: 1) Correctness (yes/no), 2) Usefulness (1-5), 3) Safety flags (none/minor/major) and a short free-text note for failure cases. The "accept rate" metric is the percent of responses labeled Correctness=yes and Usefulness>=4. We'll share an example set of 50 gold prompts so you can see how we score.

Intent tags: subset is fine — 20–30 representative prompts with tags is adequate to bootstrap class-conditional metrics.

Updated evaluation plan highlights:
- Baseline: run a 1k-sample baseline across your prompts and logs to estimate latency and cost
- Configs: run two model configurations (standard quantized vs. low-latency optimized) and compare quality/safety/cost
- Ownership: Redwood will own ingestion & baseline runs; Acme (Sam) will own annotation review and final acceptance

Kickoff: Can we do Tue Feb 10 at 10:00 AM PST or Tue Feb 10 at 2:00 PM PST? I'll send a calendar invite once you confirm.

Data handling: we'll treat the logs as sensitive and will only use them for this POC. If you prefer an additional DPA, loop procurement and we can fast-track it.

Attaching an updated POC Eval Plan with the annotation template included (redwood_poc_eval_plan-v2.pdf).

—
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
